problem.headline: Find owners in financial trouble before the broker network does.
problem.body: Bloomfield lends on and buys commercial property anywhere in the U.S. (not office). A bank has strict limits on how it can help a struggling borrower; Bloomfield has few. Reaching the borrower first means offering a loan that actually fixes the problem.
problem.story: A developer builds student housing in Ann Arbor. The opening slips from August to November, students sign leases elsewhere, the building sits empty for a year and the developer defaults. Bloomfield noticed because the project website still said "coming Winter 2026" after that date had passed.

signals.name: Construction loans that never converted
signals.built: Loan histories line up each construction loan with any permanent loan or release. A loan with neither after about 30 months is flagged, and each extension adds to the score.
signals.next: Run it on real county recorder data.

signals.name: Contractor (mechanic's) liens
signals.built: The AI reader pulls the claimant, amount and type of work from the filing with the exact quote. The scorer weights size and recency.
signals.next: Feed it real county filings (manual drop-in until each site is checked).

signals.name: UCC foreclosure sales
signals.built: The reader recognizes UCC sale notices (party, date, collateral) and the scorer weights them 30 points. WSJ pages are a weekly manual upload.
signals.next: Automatic splitting of a full newspaper page into separate notices.

signals.name: Stale or delayed opening dates
signals.built: Date rules turn phrases like "Fall 2026" into a deadline (fully tested), and the scorer flags projects that are overdue and still unopened.
signals.next: The weekly website checker and Wayback Machine history (the Scout).

signals.name: Foreclosure notices and receiverships
signals.built: The reader and scorer handle both, and the county collector runs from one settings file per county.
signals.next: Check each county site's terms before moving it from manual drop-in to automatic.

signals.name: Weak loans and lender stress
signals.built: Loaders for SEC loan filings, the Trepp screen and bank call reports are coded, and scoring passes sample tests.
signals.next: Verify SEC field names and bank-report codes against real files.

signals.name: Ten-X auctions
signals.next: The reader and scorer can already handle an auction listing; the weekly collection from Ten-X is not built. Its terms of use are checked first.

signals.name: Local news and leasing-site monitoring
signals.next: The Scout that reads approved news, developer and leasing sites each week.

signals.name: Tracking each flag through to a closed deal
signals.next: Recording what happens to every flag, so Bloomfield can measure results against its $300M goal.

tests.note: They all pass, and none needs the internet or an API key.

live_reader.note: Real model, invented documents. The run stopped at Google's free-key limit (20 requests a day).

results.accuracy: Not measured yet. Our labeled test set (about 30 documents, target about 90% of fields correct) is the next test to build.

worked: The Ann Arbor example is found automatically: stuck construction loan, stale opening date, contractor lien and a struggling lender, all on one property.
Every extracted value comes with the exact sentence it was read from, and made-up quotes are caught.
Records about the same property, loan, lender and company are linked; unsure matches go to a person.
Works with Claude, Gemini or an OpenAI-style service, with a spending cap and no private data sent.

weak_spots.what: Took a city from our instructions, not the document
weak_spots.detail: Gemini filled in a city for a document with no address. The quote check caught it.
Everything on screen is invented. We need a few anonymized deals to test on.

weak_spots.what: County and court sites are manual drop-in for now
weak_spots.detail: Each site's terms must be checked first. We never log in or get past a CAPTCHA.

weak_spots.what: Some data field names are unchecked
weak_spots.detail: SEC fields, bank-report codes and CMS dataset IDs are unchecked. Each run prints an audit.
Google retired our first model. A 30-second self-test now flags a retired name.

weak_spots.what: The free AI key allows 20 requests a day
weak_spots.detail: Enough to test, not for a weekly run over many documents. We will need a paid key.

approach.headline: We are exploring every creative route, then narrowing before Nov 17
approach.body: Finding distressed borrowers early can be approached from many angles. For now we are building and testing several in parallel. Before the final presentation we will choose: keep the full multi-signal approach, or focus on the one signal that produces the most actionable flags.

options.name: Opening-date watch
options.idea: Project websites that still say "coming soon" after the date has passed, and dates that keep moving.

options.name: Construction-loan clock
options.idea: Construction loans with no permanent loan or release recorded after their expected term.

options.name: Court and lien filings
options.idea: Contractor liens, lis pendens, foreclosure notices and receiverships at the county.

options.name: Forced and public sales
options.idea: UCC sales of ownership interests (WSJ print notices) and Ten-X auction listings.

options.name: Lender and CMBS stress
options.idea: Banks with rising commercial real estate nonaccruals, and loans with DSCR under 1.0x or on a servicer watchlist.

options.name: Creative signals
options.idea: Rent concessions growing, stalled pre-leasing, one sponsor's other projects already flagged, and banks that may sell a troubled note.

decision.when: Before Nov 17 (at the Nov 15 full run)

how_built.title: Public-records collectors
how_built.stack: Python and a shared DuckDB database
built: Collectors for county courts and recorders, SEC loan filings, bank call reports, CMS data and the Trepp screen
One settings file per county (all 3,100 are in a registry), plus statewide files
Polite by design: reads robots.txt, one request every 3 seconds per site, identifies itself, and never logs in or bypasses a CAPTCHA or paywall
A site that does not allow automation falls back to a manual drop-in folder
Every file is saved unchanged and fingerprinted (SHA-256), so nothing loads twice and a run can restart

how_built.title: AI document reader
how_built.stack: Python, schema checks, OCR; works with Claude, Gemini or OpenAI-style services
built: One wrapper for every AI call; the model is a setting, so we can switch providers in minutes
Fixed instructions and a fixed list of fields; the model only returns structured data
Every value must carry an exact quote, and the quote is checked against the document
OCR for scans, saved answers (nothing is paid for twice), a weekly spending cap, and Trepp or Bloomfield material is never sent

how_built.title: Record matcher
how_built.stack: Python; parcel, address and fuzzy name matching
built: Joins records on parcel number first, then street address, then fuzzy company names
Builds each property's loan history to see whether a construction loan was ever replaced
Links lenders to bank call reports and groups a developer's many LLCs
Uncertain matches go to a review queue instead of being guessed

how_built.title: Scoring and ranking
how_built.stack: Python; weights in a settings file Bloomfield can edit
built: Points for each independent warning sign, with the weights in one file
Signals of the same kind are capped so one story cannot inflate a score
Every score keeps its evidence trail back to the source sentence
Properties fall into three tiers: priority review, active monitoring and routine

how_built.title: Researcher view
how_built.stack: Interactive demo page today; full dashboard next
built: Ranked list with an executive summary, evidence with exact quotes, timeline and loan history
Approve, dismiss or annotate each property; the tool never contacts anyone
